availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Debug your current Claude Code session by reading the session debug log. (bundled)

availableCommands.name: audit
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Parallel exploration of docs, code, config, tests, and specs to identify cruft, then interactive triage with clear action options. (project)

availableCommands.name: codex
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to run Codex CLI (codex exec, codex resume) or wants Codex to review PRs, plans, or specs. Delegates to GPT-5.3-codex with preset reasoning modes. (project)

availableCommands.name: e2e
availableCommands.description: E2E testing patterns for kspec web UI. Use when writing Playwright tests, debugging hydration issues, or working with daemon fixtures. (project)

availableCommands.name: eval-agents
availableCommands.description: Evaluate whether AGENTS.md provides enough context for agents to make correct decisions. Spawns test agents with scenario questions and grades responses. (project)

availableCommands.name: local-review
availableCommands.description: Pre-PR quality review - verify AC coverage, test quality, E2E preference, and test isolation. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Create a pull request from current work. Handles branch creation, commits, push, and PR creation. Detects branch protection and guides through the PR workflow. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr-review
availableCommands.description: Review a PR linked to a kspec task, post findings as inline comments, and merge only when all quality gates pass. You NEVER fix code — you review and comment. If issues found, kick back to worker. (project)

availableCommands.name: release
availableCommands.description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm. (project)

availableCommands.name: svelte-5
availableCommands.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues. (project)

availableCommands.name: create-workflow
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Formalize repeatable patterns into trackable kspec workflows. Design steps, choose triggers, create loop variants, and integrate with skills.

availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Get help with kspec commands and workflows

availableCommands.name: observe
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Capture and act on systemic patterns — friction, successes, questions, and ideas. The feedback loop that drives process improvement.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Translate approved plans into specs and tasks. Import structured documents or create incrementally. Plans persist as durable artifacts with audit trail.

availableCommands.name: reflect
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured reflection at the end of work sessions. Identifies learnings, friction points, and improvements for system evolution.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Kspec-specific review gates — spec alignment, own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, and validation integration. Building block for project-specific review workflows.

availableCommands.name: task-work
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured task lifecycle — start, work, note, submit, complete. Fix cycle handling, scope management, loop mode for automation, and quality gates.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Triage inbox items systematically. Records decisions with audit trail, then executes actions. Supports inbox, observations, and automation eligibility triage.

availableCommands.name: triage-automation
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Assess and prepare tasks for automation eligibility. Verify spec coverage, acceptance criteria, and task readiness for automated agents.

availableCommands.name: triage-inbox
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Process inbox items using the record-act pattern. Categorize, promote to spec/task, merge duplicates, defer, or delete stale items with full audit trail.

availableCommands.name: writing-specs
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Create and maintain specification items — modules, features, requirements, acceptance criteria, and traits. The source of truth for what to build.

availableCommands.name: compact
availableCommands.description: Clear conversation history but keep a summary in context. Optional: /compact [instructions for summarization]

availableCommands.name: context
availableCommands.description: Show current context usage

availableCommands.description: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

availableCommands.description: Get comments from a GitHub pull request

# UI/UX Revamp

## Specs

```yaml
- title: "UI Design System"
  slug: ui-design-system
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Port imgen's design token architecture into kspec's Tailwind-based web UI.
    Map oklch color tokens, spacing, radii, z-index, typography, and animation
    keyframes as Tailwind theme extensions. Establish consistent visual language
    across all views.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The web UI app.css file
      when: |
        imgen token-contract.css values are mapped as Tailwind @theme inline extensions
      then: |
        All 16 color tokens, 4 radii, 7 spacing, 7 z-index, and 3 font families
        are available as Tailwind utility classes (e.g. bg-design-surface, border-design-border)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        A component using design tokens
      when: |
        The dark theme tokens are applied
      then: |
        oklch colors render correctly and status colors (pending=amber, in_progress=orange,
        pending_review=blue, needs_work=yellow, completed=emerald, blocked=red, cancelled=gray)
        are visually distinct
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        A view with loading states
      when: |
        Content is loading
      then: |
        Shimmer animation plays on skeleton elements, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        An active agent task card
      when: |
        The agent is working
      then: |
        Breathing/pulse animation plays on the card border, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion

- title: "App Shell and Navigation"
  slug: ui-app-shell
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Restructure the web UI layout with collapsible sidebar navigation, header bar
    with command palette and connection status, and grouped navigation sections.
    Preserve existing functionality during migration.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The web UI loaded in daemon mode
      when: |
        The app shell renders
      then: |
        A collapsible sidebar shows grouped navigation: Work (Dashboard, Tasks, Agents, Sessions),
        Specs (Specs, Plans, Validate), Capture (Inbox, Observations, Triage),
        Config (Workflows, Settings)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        Sidebar navigation items
      when: |
        Items have actionable counts (inbox items, unresolved observations, pending review tasks)
      then: |
        Badge counts display next to the relevant nav items
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The /items route
      when: |
        A user navigates to /items
      then: |
        They are redirected to /specs preserving any query parameters
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        The Observations nav item
      when: |
        There are zero unresolved observations
      then: |
        The nav item is still visible (not hidden)

- title: "Task Board (Kanban)"
  slug: ui-task-board

<script lang="ts" module>
	import { type VariantProps, tv } from "tailwind-variants";

	export const badgeVariants = tv({
		base: "focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-ring/50 aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20 dark:aria-invalid:ring-destructive/40 aria-invalid:border-destructive inline-flex w-fit shrink-0 items-center justify-center gap-1 overflow-hidden rounded-full border px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium whitespace-nowrap transition-[color,box-shadow] focus-visible:ring-[3px] [&>svg]:pointer-events-none [&>svg]:size-3",
		variants: {
			variant: {
				default:
					"bg-primary text-primary-foreground [a&]:hover:bg-primary/90 border-transparent",
				secondary:
					"bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground [a&]:hover:bg-secondary/90 border-transparent",
				destructive:
					"bg-destructive [a&]:hover:bg-destructive/90 focus-visible:ring-destructive/20 dark:focus-visible:ring-destructive/40 dark:bg-destructive/70 border-transparent text-white",
				outline: "text-foreground [a&]:hover:bg-accent [a&]:hover:text-accent-foreground",
			},
		},
		defaultVariants: {
			variant: "default",
		},
	});

	export type BadgeVariant = VariantProps<typeof badgeVariants>["variant"];
</script>

<script lang="ts">
	import type { HTMLAnchorAttributes } from "svelte/elements";
	import { cn, type WithElementRef } from "$lib/utils.js";

	let {
		ref = $bindable(null),
		href,
		class: className,
		variant = "default",
		children,
		...restProps
	}: WithElementRef<HTMLAnchorAttributes> & {
		variant?: BadgeVariant;
	} = $props();
</script>

<svelte:element
	this={href ? "a" : "span"}
	bind:this={ref}
	data-slot="badge"
	{href}
	class={cn(badgeVariants({ variant }), className)}
	{...restProps}
>
	{@render children?.()}
</svelte:element>

  - _ulid: 01KJXSVF2YKCXMJGC55G1CPBV2
    slugs:

    title: UI/UX Revamp
    content: >
      # UI/UX Revamp


      ## Specs


      ```yaml

      - title: "UI Design System"
        slug: ui-design-system
        type: feature
        parent: "@web-ui"
        description: |
          Port imgen's design token architecture into kspec's Tailwind-based web UI.
          Map oklch color tokens, spacing, radii, z-index, typography, and animation
          keyframes as Tailwind theme extensions. Establish consistent visual language
          across all views.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: |
              The web UI app.css file
            when: |
              imgen token-contract.css values are mapped as Tailwind @theme inline extensions
            then: |
              All 16 color tokens, 4 radii, 7 spacing, 7 z-index, and 3 font families
              are available as Tailwind utility classes (e.g. bg-design-surface, border-design-border)
          - id: ac-2
            given: |
              A component using design tokens
            when: |
              The dark theme tokens are applied
            then: |
              oklch colors render correctly and status colors (pending=amber, in_progress=orange,
              pending_review=blue, needs_work=yellow, completed=emerald, blocked=red, cancelled=gray)
              are visually distinct
          - id: ac-3
            given: |
              A view with loading states
            when: |
              Content is loading
            then: |
              Shimmer animation plays on skeleton elements, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion
          - id: ac-4
            given: |
              An active agent task card
            when: |
              The agent is working
            then: |
              Breathing/pulse animation plays on the card border, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion

      - title: "App Shell and Navigation"
        slug: ui-app-shell
        type: feature
        parent: "@web-ui"
        description: |
          Restructure the web UI layout with collapsible sidebar navigation, header bar
          with command palette and connection status, and grouped navigation sections.
          Preserve existing functionality during migration.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: |
              The web UI loaded in daemon mode
            when: |
              The app shell renders
            then: |
              A collapsible sidebar shows grouped navigation: Work (Dashboard, Tasks, Agents, Sessions),
              Specs (Specs, Plans, Validate), Capture (Inbox, Observations, Triage),
              Config (Workflows, Settings)
          - id: ac-2
            given: |
              Sidebar navigation items
            when: |
              Items have actionable counts (inbox items, unresolved observations, pending review tasks)
            then: |
              Badge counts display next to the relevant nav items
          - id: ac-3
            given: |
              The /items route
            when: |
              A user navigates to /items
            then: |
              They are redirected to /specs preserving any query parameters
          - id: ac-4
            given: |
              The Observations nav item
            when: |
              There are zero unresolved observations
            then: |
              The nav item is still visible (not hidden)

      - title: "Task Board (Kanban)"
        slug: ui-task-board
        type: feature
        parent: "@web-ui"
        description: |
          Kanban-style task board with columns mapping to kspec task states.
          Active Fleet row shows currently running agent work with live output.
          Task cards show key metadata, clicking opens detail modal.
          Not drag-and-drop — tasks transition via agents/CLI.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: |
              Tasks in various states
            when: |
              The task board renders
            then: |
              Tasks are distributed into columns: Backlog (pending, manual_only/unassessed),
              Ready (pending, eligible), In Progress (in_progress, needs_work),
              Review (pending_review), Done (completed recent), with blocked and cancelled
              handled as sections/indicators
          - id: ac-2
            given: |
              A task card on the board
            when: |
              The card renders
            then: |
              It shows priority badge, tag chips, title, slug (mono), spec ref link,
              and metadata footer (notes count, dependency count, age)
          - id: ac-3
            given: |
              A task card
            when: |
              The user clicks it
            then: |
              A detail modal opens showing full task info: title, description, status,
              priority, type, spec ref, tags, dependencies, blocked-by, notes, todos,
              automation status, VCS info (branch, PR link), plan ref, session link
          - id: ac-4
            given: |
              Agents actively working on tasks (dispatch running)
            when: |
              The task board renders
            then: |
              An Active Fleet row appears at the top showing cards with task title,
              agent name, elapsed time with pulse indicator, and last few lines of output
          - id: ac-5
            given: |
              The task board with WebSocket connected
            when: |
              A task state changes
            then: |
              The board updates in real-time without page refresh
          - id: ac-6
            given: |
              The task detail modal in daemon mode
            when: |
              The user clicks action buttons (Start, Submit, Complete, Block, Add Note)
            then: |
              The corresponding task transition or mutation is executed via API

      - title: "Session Stream View"
        slug: ui-session-stream
        type: feature
        parent: "@web-ui"
        description: |
          View for watching agent work — both historical and live. Renders structured
          session events (messages, tool calls, thinking blocks) from events.jsonl.
          Live sessions show streaming text with periodic structured refresh.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: |
              A completed session with events.jsonl
            when: |
              The user navigates to /sessions/:id
            then: |
              The session events render as structured blocks: agent messages (markdown),
              tool calls (collapsible with icon, input/output, timing), and thinking blocks
              (collapsed by default, expandable)
          - id: ac-2
            given: |
              An active session with streaming output
            when: |
              The user views the session
            then: |
              Live text streams in real-time via agent_text_chunk WebSocket events,
              with periodic structured refresh from events.jsonl
          - id: ac-3
            given: |
              The session stream view
            when: |
              New content arrives while auto-scrolling
            then: |
              The view auto-scrolls to follow new content, pauses when user scrolls up
              (>100px from bottom), and resumes when scrolled back. A "jump to bottom"
              button appears when paused.
          - id: ac-4
            given: |
              The session stream view
            when: |
              A session context panel is shown on the left
            then: |
              It displays session metadata, spec context with AC checklist,
              files changed during session, and budget info

      - title: "Agent and Dispatch View"
        slug: ui-agent-dispatch
        type: feature
        parent: "@web-ui"
        description: |
          View showing agent definitions, dispatch status (running/stopped),
          and active invocations with links to session streams.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: |
              The /agents route
            when: |
              Agent definitions exist in meta
            then: |
              Each agent shows name, triggers, active invocation count, and completed count
          - id: ac-2
            given: |
              The dispatch engine is running
            when: |
              The agents page renders
            then: |
              Dispatch status shows as running with a stop button, and active invocations
              show task ref, elapsed time, and link to session stream
          - id: ac-3
            given: |
              The dispatch engine is stopped
            when: |
              The agents page renders
            then: |
              Dispatch status shows as stopped with no active invocations

      - title: "Session History"
        slug: ui-session-history
        type: feature
        parent: "@web-ui"
        description: |
          List view of past agent sessions with filtering and navigation to session detail.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: |
              Sessions exist on disk
            when: |
              The user navigates to /sessions
            then: |
              A list of sessions shows ID, agent type, task ref, status,
              duration, and age, sorted by most recent first
          - id: ac-2
            given: |
              The session list
            when: |
              The user clicks a session
            then: |
              They navigate to /sessions/:id showing the session stream view

      - title: "Enhanced Inbox View"
        slug: ui-inbox-enhanced
        type: feature
        parent: "@web-ui"
        description: |
          Enhanced inbox with triage status inline, quick actions, filtering, and bulk selection.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: |
              Inbox items with varying triage states
            when: |
              The inbox view renders
            then: |
              Each item shows triage status inline (untriaged/triaged/acted_on)
              with quick triage action links
          - id: ac-2
            given: |
              The inbox view
            when: |
              The user applies filters (status, tags, age)
            then: |
              The list filters accordingly

      - title: "Plans View"
        slug: ui-plans-view
        type: feature
        parent: "@web-ui"
        description: |
          View for browsing plan records with progress tracking via linked specs and tasks.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: |
              Plan records exist
            when: |

      - _ulid: 01KJXSVF2YDSBAM76XMSQHBCFX
        created_at: 2026-03-05T01:30:02.718Z
        author: "@claude"
        content: |-
          Implementation notes:

          #### ui-design-system
          Set up the isolated clone first. Port imgen's full token-contract.css into
          Tailwind @theme inline in app.css. Start with the token bridge pilot on the
          dashboard page to validate the approach before touching other views. Create
          tokens.css, animations.css, typography.css in lib/ds/. Establish loading
          skeleton and error boundary patterns.

          #### ui-app-shell
          Restructure +layout.svelte with new sidebar component. Migrate existing
          Sidebar.svelte to grouped navigation. Add /items -> /specs redirect.
          Fix Observations nav visibility bug. Migrate taskDetailStore from Svelte 4
          to Svelte 5 runes. Consolidate three existing task detail implementations.
          Ensure all existing routes still work.

          #### ui-task-board
          Prerequisite: daemon must return type and automation in task list API response
          (quick fix to packages/daemon/src/routes/tasks.ts). Add needs_work to status
          color/label maps. Build KanbanBoard, KanbanColumn, TaskCard, TaskDetailModal,
          ActiveFleetRow components. Wire to tasks:updates WebSocket topic. Build task
          mutation endpoints in daemon (submit, complete, block) for detail modal actions.

          #### ui-session-stream
          Prerequisite: build GET /api/sessions and GET /api/sessions/:id/events daemon
          endpoints. Two-tier rendering: structured events from events.jsonl for history,
          agent_text_chunk WS for live text. Build SessionStream, ChatMessage,
          ToolCallView, ThinkingBlock components. Implement auto-scroll with pause/resume.
          Port patterns from kynetic-internal's ChatPanel.

          #### ui-agent-dispatch
          Uses existing GET /api/agent/dispatch/status and GET /api/agent/status endpoints.
          Subscribe to agents WS topic for real-time updates. Build AgentList,
          DispatchStatus, InvocationCard components.

          #### ui-session-history
          Depends on GET /api/sessions endpoint from ui-session-stream work.
          Build SessionList with filtering. Link to session stream view.

          #### ui-inbox-enhanced
          Enhance existing inbox view. Add triage status from existing triage API.
          Add filter controls. Keep existing add/delete functionality.

          #### ui-plans-view
          Prerequisite: build GET /api/plans daemon endpoint (wrap existing loadAllPlans).
          Build PlanList with progress calculation from linked task statuses.

          #### ui-validation-view
          Uses existing GET /api/validate and GET /api/alignment endpoints.
          Build ValidationSummary, AlignmentStats, IssueList components.

          #### ui-dashboard-overview
          Build last. Uses data from tasks, inbox, observations, validation APIs.
          Active work section reuses ActiveFleetRow from task board.
          No aggregated activity API needed — merge recent data client-side.

_ulid: 01KFHMF5ZS4RD70JBQNGBQJVFY
slugs:
  - web-ui
title: Web UI System
type: module
status:
  maturity: draft
  implementation: implemented
description: >
  Web-based interface for viewing, editing, and managing kspec state. Includes three deployment
  modes:

  1. Local daemon mode - Elysia.js server on Bun with WebSocket for real-time updates

  2. Web dashboard - SvelteKit + shadcn-svelte for full CRUD operations

  3. GitHub Pages export - Static JSON snapshot with read-only SPA for public sharing


  Tech stack: Elysia.js, Bun runtime, WebSocket (not SSE), SvelteKit, shadcn-svelte.

  Distribution via bun build --compile for portable executables.
tags:
  - web
  - ui
  - daemon
  - elysia
  - bun
depends_on: []
implements: []
relates_to: []
tests: []
traits: []
notes: []
features:
  - _ulid: 01KFHMFGD2563NGHJWPPXGN9CB
    slugs:
      - daemon-server
    title: Daemon Server Mode
    type: feature
    tags:
      - server
      - websocket
      - elysia
    description: >
      Long-running Elysia.js server on Bun runtime that exposes kspec state via HTTP API and
      WebSocket

      for real-time updates. Binds to localhost only for security. Supports foreground and
      background

      modes with PID file management. Includes heartbeat ping/pong for connection health monitoring.
    depends_on: []
    implements: []
    relates_to: []
    tests: []
    traits:
      - "@trait-json-output"
      - "@trait-error-guidance"
      - "@trait-shadow-commit"
      - "@trait-localhost-security"
      - "@trait-websocket-protocol"
    notes: []
    created: 2026-01-22T01:18:09.314Z
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: ac-1
        given: kspec is installed
        when: user runs 'kspec serve'
        then: Elysia HTTP server starts on configurable port (default 3456) binding to localhost only
      - id: ac-2
        given: daemon is starting
        when: server binds to network interface
        then: only accepts connections from 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (IPv6 localhost)
      - id: ac-3
        given: connection attempt from non-localhost IP
        when: request received
        then: connection rejected with 403 Forbidden
      - id: ac-4
        given: daemon is running
        when: any .kspec/*.yaml file changes
        then: connected WebSocket clients receive update event via topic subscription
      - id: ac-5
        given: file watching is active
        when: rapid changes occur (< 500ms apart)
        then: events are debounced and aggregated into single notification
      - id: ac-6
        given: watched file has YAML parse error
        when: change detected
        then: error logged and WebSocket broadcasts error event (daemon does not crash)
      - id: ac-7
        given: .kspec directory becomes inaccessible
        when: watcher encounters error
        then: daemon logs error and attempts recovery with exponential backoff
      - id: ac-8
        given: Bun fs.watch fails or misses events
        when: reliability issue detected
        then: automatically fall back to Chokidar file watcher
      - id: ac-9
        given: daemon is running
        when: user runs 'kspec serve --daemon'
        then: process detaches to background, writes PID to .kspec/.daemon.pid, CLI returns immediately
      - id: ac-10
        given: daemon is running in background
        when: user runs 'kspec serve stop'
        then: daemon shuts down gracefully, removes PID file, closes all WebSocket connections
      - id: ac-11
        given: daemon is running
        when: GET /api/health is called
        then: returns {status, uptime, connections, version} JSON
      - id: ac-12
        given: daemon receives SIGTERM or SIGINT
        when: shutdown signal received
        then: graceful shutdown (flush pending messages, close connections, save state)
      - id: ac-13
        given: WebSocket connection established
        when: 30 seconds pass without activity
        then: server sends ping frame
      - id: ac-14
        given: ping was sent
        when: no pong received within 90 seconds
        then: connection closed with code 1001
      - id: ac-15
        given: Elysia server is configured
        when: routes are registered
        then: use plugin pattern for middleware (CORS, logging, validation)
      - id: ac-16
        given: daemon code is ready
        when: bun build --compile runs
        then: produces standalone executable without requiring Bun installation
      - id: ac-17
        given: daemon is running with web UI built
        when: browser opens http://localhost:<port>/
        then: serves the built web UI assets (SvelteKit static build) as the root route
    status:
      maturity: draft
      implementation: in_progress
    features:
      - _ulid: 01KJP2768T96S8870BH36ZE76K
        slugs:
          - daemon-agent-dispatch
        title: Daemon Agent Dispatch Integration
        type: feature
        tags: []
        description: |
          Agent dispatch API routes in the daemon, enhanced file watcher with
          task state diffing for change detection, CLI event emission endpoint,
          and WebSocket broadcasts for agent invocation status.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: |
              The daemon is running with dispatch enabled
            when: |
              The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml
            then: |
              The watcher parses the new task states, diffs against the
              previously cached states, and emits state change events to
              the dispatch engine for each detected transition
          - id: ac-2
            given: |
              A CLI command changes task state (e.g. kspec task start)
            when: |
              The daemon is running
            then: |
              The CLI posts a JSON event to POST /api/agent/events containing
              task_id, previous_status, new_status, and timestamp
          - id: ac-3
            given: |
              The daemon receives a state change event matching dispatch rules
            when: |
              The dispatch engine processes it
            then: |
              The agent is dispatched and a status event is broadcast on the
              agents WebSocket topic
          - id: ac-4
            given: |
              A WebSocket client subscribes to agent status updates
            when: |
              An agent invocation starts, completes, or fails
            then: |
              A broadcast event is sent containing session_id, agent_id,
              task_id, status, and timestamp
          - id: ac-5
            given: |
              GET /api/agent/status is called
            when: |
              The dispatch engine is running
            then: |
              Returns JSON with active invocations array, queue depth number,
              dispatch_enabled boolean, and agent_definitions array
          - id: ac-6
            given: |
              POST /api/agent/dispatch is called with action start or stop
            when: |
              The request is from localhost
            then: |
              The dispatch engine starts or stops and returns JSON with the
              new dispatch_enabled state
          - id: ac-7
            given: |
              The daemon is not running
            when: |
              A CLI command changes task state
            then: |
              The event emission POST fails silently with no error to the
              user — dispatch requires a running daemon
          - id: ac-8
            given: The dispatch engine runs an agent invocation
            when: The agent produces text output (agent_message_chunk events)
            then: The daemon broadcasts each text chunk on the agents WebSocket topic with type
              agent_text_chunk, session_id, agent_id, task_id, text, and timestamp
        depends_on: []
        implements: []
        relates_to: []
        tests: []
        traits:
          - "@trait-api-endpoint"
          - "@trait-localhost-security"
          - "@trait-websocket-protocol"
        notes: []
        created: 2026-03-02T01:22:20.058Z
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: implemented
    requirements:
      - _ulid: 01KJRZWDCC8W2WT0Q3A9CZAAGY
        slugs:
          - daemon-web-ui-bundle
        title: Web UI assets bundled in npm package
        type: requirement
        tags: []
        depends_on: []
        implements: []
        relates_to: []
        tests: []
        traits: []
        notes: []
        created: 2026-03-03T04:39:13.036Z
        description: The kspec npm package bundles the pre-built web UI static assets so the daemon can
          serve the web UI when installed in any project, without requiring a local web UI build.
          The build pipeline copies packages/web-ui/build to dist/web-ui/, and resolveWebUiPath
          falls back to that location relative to the daemon module.
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: npm run build is executed
            when: build completes
            then: packages/web-ui/build output is copied to dist/web-ui/ in the package
          - id: ac-2
            given: kspec is installed in a project with no local web UI build
            when: daemon starts and resolves web UI path
            then: resolveWebUiPath returns the bundled dist/web-ui/ path relative to the daemon module location
          - id: ac-3
            given: kspec is installed as an npm package in a non-monorepo project
            when: browser opens http://localhost:3456/
            then: daemon serves the bundled web UI and returns HTTP 200 with HTML content
          - id: ac-4
            given: an explicit webUiDir option or WEB_UI_DIR env var or local packages/web-ui/build is present
            when: daemon starts
            then: the explicit or local path takes precedence over the bundled dist/web-ui/ fallback
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: implemented
      - _ulid: 01KJTVMGPNP3HN9B9SRF6MEER7
        slugs:
          - ws-disconnect-lifecycle-cleanup
        title: WebSocket Disconnect Lifecycle Cleanup
        type: requirement
        tags:
          - daemon
          - websocket
          - reliability
        description: Ensure daemon WebSocket disconnect handling is accurate for abnormal closes. Disconnect
          events must reliably identify the same session created on connect, remove that session
          from in-memory registries, and prevent stale heartbeat/client counts after client
          disconnect or process termination.
        depends_on: []
        implements: []
        relates_to: []
        tests: []
        traits: []
        notes: []
        created: 2026-03-03T22:03:28.854Z
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: multiple clients are connected and one disconnects

    slugs:
      - multi-directory-daemon
    title: Multi-Directory Daemon Architecture
    type: feature
    tags:
      - daemon
      - architecture
      - multi-project
    description: |
      Extends the daemon server to support multiple kspec projects simultaneously from a single
      daemon process. Projects are identified via X-Kspec-Dir HTTP header. Enables E2E testing
      with isolated fixtures and multi-project development workflows.

      Key architectural changes:
      - Global daemon with PID/port files at ~/.config/kspec/
      - Project context caching with on-demand registration
      - Per-project file watchers
      - WebSocket connections bound to specific projects

      BREAKING CHANGE: PID/port files move from .kspec/.daemon.pid to ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid
    depends_on:
      - "@daemon-server"
      - "@api-contract"
    implements: []
    relates_to:
      - "@cli-serve-commands"
    tests: []
    traits:
      - "@trait-localhost-security"
      - "@trait-websocket-protocol"
    notes:
      - _ulid: 01KFQ84FVZB2CWH7Y4GPQR8M9N
        created_at: 2026-01-24T06:00:00.000Z
        author: "@claude"
        content: |
          Design decisions:
          - X-Kspec-Dir header for project selection (clean URLs, easy for clients)
          - Single bundled web UI (consistent version across projects)
          - On-demand project registration (auto-register on first request)
          - No memory limit on cached projects (keep until restart)
          - Global PID at ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid
          - Per-project file watchers
          - Backwards compatible (no header = startup cwd project if valid)
    created: 2026-01-24T06:00:00.000Z
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: ac-1
        given: daemon is running
        when: request includes X-Kspec-Dir header with valid absolute path
        then: daemon uses that project's context for the request
      - id: ac-2
        given: daemon started from directory with .kspec/
        when: request has no X-Kspec-Dir header
        then: daemon uses startup directory's project as default
      - id: ac-3
        given: daemon started from directory without .kspec/
        when: request without X-Kspec-Dir arrives
        then: return 400 with error "No default project configured. Specify X-Kspec-Dir header."
      - id: ac-4
        given: request specifies unknown project path
        when: path is valid kspec project
        then: daemon auto-registers and caches project context
      - id: ac-5
        given: request specifies invalid path (no .kspec/)
        when: request processed
        then: return 400 with error "Invalid kspec project - .kspec/ not found at <path>"
      - id: ac-6
        given: X-Kspec-Dir header value
        when: path is relative
        then: reject with 400 and error "Path must be absolute"
      - id: ac-7
        given: X-Kspec-Dir header value
        when: path contains ".." segments
        then: reject with 400 and error "Path must not contain parent traversal"
      - id: ac-8
        given: X-Kspec-Dir header value
        when: normalized path differs from provided path
        then: use normalized path for registration (resolve "." segments, remove trailing slashes, do NOT
          resolve symlinks)
      - id: ac-8b
        given: X-Kspec-Dir points to path with insufficient read permissions
        when: request processed
        then: return 403 with error "Permission denied - cannot read <path>"
      - id: ac-9
        given: no daemon running
        when: kspec serve start runs from any directory
        then: daemon starts and writes PID to ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid and port to
          ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port
      - id: ac-9b
        given: ~/.config/kspec/ does not exist
        when: daemon starts
        then: create directory with mode 0755 before writing PID/port files
      - id: ac-9c
        given: ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port exists but contains invalid content
        when: CLI reads port
        then: return error "Invalid daemon port file" and suggest "kspec serve stop && kspec serve start"
      - id: ac-10
        given: daemon running on port 3456
        when: kspec serve start runs from different directory
        then: command exits with success and outputs "Daemon already running on port 3456" (no second
          instance started)
      - id: ac-10b
        given: two kspec serve start commands run concurrently (neither has written PID yet)
        when: both check for running daemon
        then: only one daemon starts (use file lock on PID file)
      - id: ac-11
        given: daemon running
        when: kspec serve stop runs from any directory
        then: daemon stops and removes global PID and port files
      - id: ac-12
        given: daemon running
        when: kspec serve status runs
        then: shows daemon status with port, uptime, and list of registered projects with their paths
      - id: ac-13
        given: CLI needs to connect to daemon
        when: daemon is running
        then: CLI reads port from ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port
      - id: ac-14
        given: daemon restarts
        when: first request for a project arrives
        then: project is re-registered automatically (same as initial registration)
      - id: ac-15
        given: daemon running with registered projects
        when: daemon restarts
        then: registered project list is empty (no persistence across restarts)
      - id: ac-16
        given: two concurrent requests for unregistered project with same path
        when: processed
        then: both succeed and share the same registered project context (no duplicate watchers)
      - id: ac-17
        given: project is registered
        when: files change in project's .kspec/
        then: file watcher triggers events scoped to that project
      - id: ac-18
        given: multiple projects registered
        when: Project A changes
        then: only Project A's WebSocket subscribers receive updates
      - id: ac-19
        given: project watcher creation fails due to OS limits (ulimit)
        when: error occurs
        then: project registration fails with 503 and error "Unable to watch project - resource limit
          reached"
      - id: ac-20
        given: registered project's .kspec/ directory is deleted
        when: next request arrives for that project
        then: return 404 and unregister project automatically
      - id: ac-21
        given: WebSocket client connects with X-Kspec-Dir header during handshake
        when: connection established
        then: connection is bound to that project for its lifetime and only receives events from that
          project
      - id: ac-21b
        given: WebSocket connection is established and bound to project
        when: client attempts to change project
        then: project binding is immutable - client must disconnect and reconnect with new header
      - id: ac-22
        given: WebSocket client connects without X-Kspec-Dir header
        when: default project exists
        then: connection is bound to default project
      - id: ac-23
        given: WebSocket client connects without X-Kspec-Dir header
        when: no default project
        then: connection is rejected with close code 4000 and reason "No project specified"
      - id: ac-24
        given: multi-project mode

        then: response data is scoped to the request's project (no cross-project data leakage)
      - id: ac-25

      - id: ac-26

      - id: ac-28
        given: GET /api/projects

      - id: ac-29
        given: POST /api/projects
        when: called with {path string} body

      - id: ac-30
        given: DELETE /api/projects/:encodedPath

## Exploration Report: packages/web-ui/ Directory Structure

export default {

  - Example: `buttonVariants` in button.svelte with variant/size props
  - Example: `badgeVariants` with semantic variants (default, secondary, destructive, outline)

**Class Merging:**
- All components use `cn()` to safely merge classes

- Uses `.dark` class selector (not media query)
- OKLch color space ensures consistent dark mode contrast

### 9. **Existing Architecture Strengths**

✓ Modern Tailwind v4 with CSS-in-JS-like flexibility
✓ Comprehensive color token system with dark mode
✓ Established variant patterns via tailwind-variants
✓ bit-ui foundation components (composable, accessible)

## UI Revamp Plan - Complete Architectural Context

I've thoroughly reviewed the UI/UX revamp plan for the kynetic-spec project. Here's the complete architectural context:

### Overview

The UI revamp plan (plan ID: `01KJXSVF2YKCXMJGC55G1CPBV2`) defines a comprehensive redesign of the web UI across 10 major feature areas, with supporting design system and component architecture.

---

### Design System Architecture

**File:** `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/app.css`

**Token Structure:**
- **Color System**: OKLCH color space for perceptual uniformity
- **16 Design Tokens** (oklch format with lightness/chroma/hue):
  - Background, Foreground, Card, Card-foreground
  - Popover, Popover-foreground
  - Primary, Primary-foreground
  - Secondary, Secondary-foreground
  - Muted, Muted-foreground
  - Accent, Accent-foreground
  - Destructive
  - Border, Input, Ring

- **5 Chart Colors** (for data visualization)
- **8 Sidebar-specific Tokens** (theme variants for navigation)

**Dark Theme Support:**
The tokens automatically swap when the `.dark` class is applied, providing full dark mode support with oklch values optimized for contrast and readability.

**Current Status:**
- Tailwind @theme inline extensions already mapped (lines 76-112 in app.css)
- Variables system uses CSS custom properties for dynamic theming
- Base layer styling established (border-border, outline-ring/50, bg-background, text-foreground)

**Spacing:** CSS variables calculated as `--radius: 0.625rem` with 4 radius tokens:
- `--radius-sm` (0.625rem - 4px)
- `--radius-md` (0.625rem - 2px)
- `--radius-lg` (0.625rem)
- `--radius-xl` (0.625rem + 4px)

**Status Color Mappings** (from spec):
- `pending` = amber
- `in_progress` = orange
- `pending_review` = blue
- `needs_work` = yellow
- `completed` = emerald
- `blocked` = red
- `cancelled` = gray

**Animations:**
- Shimmer animation for skeleton loaders (gated behind `prefers-reduced-motion`)
- Breathing/pulse animation for active agent task cards (gated behind `prefers-reduced-motion`)

---

### Component Architecture

**Current Component Structure** (`/packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/`):

**Layout Components:**
- `Sidebar.svelte` - Collapsible navigation sidebar with grouped sections
- `MobileNav.svelte` - Bottom navigation for mobile (< 768px)
- `CommandPalette.svelte` - Global command/search palette (Cmd+K / Ctrl+K)
- `ConnectionStatus.svelte` - WebSocket connection indicator

**Feature Components:**
- `ItemDetail.svelte` - Spec item detail viewer
- `ItemTree.svelte` - Hierarchical spec item tree
- `TaskList.svelte` - Task list with filtering
- `TaskDetail.svelte` - Task detail view (legacy)
- `TaskDetailPanel.svelte` - Task detail slide-over panel
- `TaskFilters.svelte` - Filter controls for task list
- `ProjectSelector.svelte` - Multi-project selector (for multi-directory daemon mode)

**UI Primitives** (`/lib/components/ui/`):
- Shadcn-svelte components: Accordion, Badge, Button, Card, Dialog, Dropdown-menu, Input, Label, Popover, Select, Sheet, Sidebar, Table, Tabs, Toast, Tooltip, etc.

**Banner Components:**
- `ReadOnlyBanner.svelte` - Static mode indicator with "data freshness" timestamp

---

### App Shell and Navigation

**Current Implementation:**
- Main layout file: `+layout.svelte` (SvelteKit root layout)
- Uses `SidebarProvider` and `SidebarInset` from shadcn-svelte
- Desktop sidebar hidden on mobile (`hidden md:block`)
- Responsive inset with main content area (`flex-1 overflow-auto`)

**Sidebar Grouping** (planned):
```
Work
  - Dashboard
  - Tasks
  - Agents
  - Sessions

Specs
  - Specs
  - Plans
  - Validate

Capture
  - Inbox
  - Observations
  - Triage

Config
  - Workflows
  - Settings
```

**Badge Counts:**
- Inbox items count
- Unresolved observations count
- Pending review task count

**Current Routes:**
- `/` - Dashboard
- `/items` - Specs (should redirect `/items` → `/specs`)
- `/tasks` - Task list
- `/inbox` - Inbox
- `/observations` - Observations
- `/triage` - Triage view

---

### Feature Specifications (10 Areas)

#### 1. **UI Design System** (`@ui-design-system`)
- Port imgen's design token architecture into Tailwind
- Map oklch color tokens, spacing, radii, z-index, typography, animation keyframes
- **AC Focus**: 16 color tokens, 4 radii, 7 spacing, 7 z-index, 3 font families as Tailwind utilities
- Dark theme with status colors
- Loading shimmer animations
- Agent task card breathing/pulse animations

#### 2. **App Shell and Navigation** (`@ui-app-shell`)
- Restructure +layout.svelte with grouped sidebar navigation
- Migrate Sidebar.svelte to grouped sections
- Add `/items` → `/specs` redirect
- Fix Observations nav visibility bug
- Migrate taskDetailStore from Svelte 4 to Svelte 5 runes
- Consolidate 3 existing task detail implementations

#### 3. **Task Board (Kanban)** (`@ui-task-board`)
- Kanban-style columns mapping to task states:
  - **Backlog**: pending (manual_only/unassessed)
  - **Ready**: pending (eligible)
  - **In Progress**: in_progress, needs_work
  - **Review**: pending_review
  - **Done**: completed (recent)
  - **Blocked/Cancelled**: sections/indicators

- **Task Card Elements**: Priority badge, tag chips, title, slug (monospace), spec ref link, metadata footer (notes count, dependency count, age)
- **Detail Modal**: Full task info with title, description, status, priority, type, spec ref, tags, dependencies, blocked-by, notes, todos, automation status, VCS info, plan ref, session link
- **Active Fleet Row**: Shows currently running agent tasks with title, agent name, elapsed time (with pulse indicator), last few lines of output
- **Real-time Updates**: WebSocket-driven board updates via `tasks:updates` topic
- **Mutations**: Task action buttons (Start, Submit, Complete, Block, Add Note) execute via API

**Daemon Prerequisite**: 
- Daemon must return `type` and `automation` fields in task list API response
- Build components: KanbanBoard, KanbanColumn, TaskCard, TaskDetailModal, ActiveFleetRow

#### 4. **Session Stream View** (`@ui-session-stream`)
- View for watching agent work (historical and live)
- Renders structured session events from `events.jsonl`
- **Two-tier rendering**:
  - Structured events from `events.jsonl` (history)
  - `agent_text_chunk` WebSocket events (live text)
  
- **Event Types**: Agent messages (markdown), tool calls (collapsible with icon, input/output, timing), thinking blocks (collapsed by default)
- **Live Streaming**: Real-time text via WebSocket with periodic structured refresh
- **Auto-scroll**: Follow new content, pause when user scrolls up (>100px from bottom), resume when scrolled back, "jump to bottom" button when paused
- **Session Context Panel**: Session metadata, spec context with AC checklist, files changed, budget info

**Daemon Prerequisites**:
- Build GET `/api/sessions` and GET `/api/sessions/:id/events` endpoints
- Build components: SessionStream, ChatMessage, ToolCallView, ThinkingBlock

#### 5. **Agent and Dispatch View** (`@ui-agent-dispatch`)
- Shows agent definitions, dispatch status (running/stopped)
- Active invocations with links to session streams
- Uses existing GET `/api/agent/dispatch/status` and GET `/api/agent/status` endpoints
- Subscribe to `agents` WebSocket topic for real-time updates
- Components: AgentList, DispatchStatus, InvocationCard

#### 6. **Session History** (`@ui-session-history`)
- List view of past agent sessions
- Display: ID, agent type, task ref, status, duration, age (sorted by most recent first)
- Filtering support
- Navigate to session detail (session stream view)
- Depends on GET `/api/sessions` endpoint from ui-session-stream work

#### 7. **Enhanced Inbox View** (`@ui-inbox-enhanced`)
- Triage status inline (untriaged/triaged/acted_on)
- Quick triage action links
- Filter controls (status, tags, age)
- Keep existing add/delete functionality

#### 8. **Plans View** (`@ui-plans-view`)
- Browse plan records with progress tracking
- Display: Title, status, creation date, linked spec/task counts, progress (based on task completion)
- **Daemon Prerequisite**: Build GET `/api/plans` endpoint (wrap existing loadAllPlans)

#### 9. **Validation and Alignment View** (`@ui-validation-view`)
- Validation results, alignment statistics, issues
- Summary: Error count, warning count, valid item count
- Alignment section: Spec coverage %, AC coverage %, orphaned tasks/specs counts
- Issues list grouped by severity
- Uses existing GET `/api/validate` and GET `/api/alignment` endpoints

#### 10. **Dashboard Overview** (`@ui-dashboard-overview`)
- Home view: "What's happening right now?"
- **Active work section**: Currently running agent tasks
- **Status summary**: Clickable count cards per status
- **Needs-attention section**: Aggregates:
  - Untriaged inbox items
  - Unresolved observations
  - Validation warnings
  - Blocked tasks
- Build last (reuses ActiveFleetRow from task board)
- No aggregated activity API needed; merge recent data client-side

---

### Implementation Notes

**Design System:**
- Set up isolated clone first
- Port imgen's full `token-contract.css` into Tailwind @theme inline in app.css
- Start with token bridge pilot on dashboard page to validate approach
- Create modular CSS files: `tokens.css`, `animations.css`, `typography.css` in `lib/ds/`
- Establish loading skeleton and error boundary patterns

**App Shell:**
- Restructure `+layout.svelte` with new sidebar component
- Migrate existing Sidebar.svelte to grouped navigation
- Add `/items` → `/specs` redirect
- Fix Observations nav visibility bug
- Migrate taskDetailStore from Svelte 4 to Svelte 5 runes
- Consolidate three existing task detail implementations
- Ensure all existing routes continue working

**Daemon API Changes Required:**
- Task list API: Add `type` and `automation` fields to response
- Task mutations: Build POST endpoints for `/api/tasks/:ref/start`, `/api/tasks/:ref/submit`, `/api/tasks/:ref/complete`, `/api/tasks/:ref/block`
- Sessions: Add GET `/api/sessions` and GET `/api/sessions/:id/events`
- Plans: Add GET `/api/plans` endpoint

**WebSocket Topics:**
- `tasks:updates` - Task state changes
- `agents` - Agent dispatch status and text chunks
- `files:updates` - File change notifications

**Dependencies Between Features:**
```
ui-design-system (foundation)
├── ui-app-shell
├── ui-task-board
├── ui-dashboard-overview
└── ui-session-stream
    ├── ui-session-history
    └── ui-agent-dispatch
```

---

### Technology Stack

- **Framework**: SvelteKit (Svelte 5 with runes)
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS 4 with @theme inline
- **UI Components**: shadcn-svelte
- **Color Space**: OKLCH (perceptual)
- **Real-time**: WebSocket (topic-based pub/sub)
- **State Management**: Svelte runes (reactive)
- **Animation**: CSS keyframes with `prefers-reduced-motion` gates

---

### Key Acceptance Criteria Highlights

1. **Design System**: 16 color tokens, 4 radii, 7 spacing values, 7 z-index, 3 font families available as Tailwind utilities
2. **Dark Theme**: Status colors visually distinct (amber, orange, blue, yellow, emerald, red, gray)
3. **Real-time Updates**: WebSocket-driven without page refresh
4. **Mobile Responsive**: Sidebar → bottom nav on small screens, detail panels on large screens (≥1024px)
5. **Command Palette**: Global search (Cmd+K / Ctrl+K) with results grouped by type
6. **WebSocket Resilience**: Exponential backoff reconnection (1s, 2s, 4s... max 30s), sequence deduplication
7. **Agent Work Visibility**: Active Fleet row with elapsed time, pulse indicator, live output streaming

---

### File Locations

- **Plan Record**: `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/.kspec/project.plans.yaml` (lines 7613-8133)
- **App CSS (Design Tokens)**: `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/app.css`
- **Layout**: `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/routes/+layout.svelte`
- **Tailwind Config**: `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/tailwind.config.js`
- **Components**: `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/`
- **UI Primitives**: `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/ui/`

---

This comprehensive plan provides a complete redesign roadmap with clear feature boundaries, specific acceptance criteria, daemon API requirements, and implementation guidance for modernizing the kspec web UI with a cohesive design system and improved user experience.

/*
 * Token Contract Reference
 *
 * This file documents the CSS custom properties that every design theme.css
 * must define for shared design-system components to render correctly.
 *
 * DO NOT import this file — it exists only as documentation.
 * Each design defines its own values in its theme.css scoped under [data-design="N"].
 *
 * Colors (16):
 *   --design-bg
 *   --design-fg
 *   --design-card
 *   --design-card-fg
 *   --design-primary        — Active/committed: buttons, selected chips, CTAs, progress
 *   --design-primary-fg     — Text on primary backgrounds
 *   --design-secondary
 *   --design-secondary-fg
 *   --design-muted
 *   --design-muted-fg
 *   --design-accent         — Decorative + hover: eyebrows, markers, glow, shimmer, hover states
 *   --design-accent-fg      — Text on accent backgrounds
 *
 * Interaction language:
 *   neutral → accent (hover/anticipation) → primary (active/selected/committed)
 *   Buttons, chips, nav links use accent on hover. Primary on active/selected state.
 *   --design-destructive
 *   --design-border
 *   --design-input
 *   --design-ring
 *
 * Radii (4):
 *   --design-radius-sm
 *   --design-radius-md
 *   --design-radius-lg
 *   --design-radius-xl
 *
 * Spacing (7):
 *   --design-spacing-xs     — 0.25rem (4px)
 *   --design-spacing-sm     — 0.5rem (8px)
 *   --design-spacing-md     — 1rem (16px)
 *   --design-spacing-lg     — 1.5rem (24px)
 *   --design-spacing-xl     — 2rem (32px)
 *   --design-spacing-2xl    — 3rem (48px)
 *   --design-spacing-3xl    — 4rem (64px)
 *
 * Z-Index Layers (7):
 *   --design-z-base         — 0 (default layer)
 *   --design-z-dropdown     — 10 (dropdown menus)
 *   --design-z-sticky       — 20 (sticky nav, pinned elements)
 *   --design-z-overlay      — 30 (backdrop overlays)
 *   --design-z-modal        — 40 (dialogs, lightbox)
 *   --design-z-popover      — 50 (tooltips, popovers on top of modals)
 *   --design-z-toast        — 60 (toast notifications, always on top)
 *
 * Fonts (3, injected by next/font in layout):
 *   --font-design-primary
 *   --font-design-secondary
 *   --font-design-mono
 */
